title: What numbers fill the top of these pyramids?
description: Three number pyramids with only the bottom row filled are completed, using the rule that each block is the sum of the two blocks directly below it. Keeko doubts that the top of the second pyramid is the sum of its whole bottom row.
teaching_notes: One idea: each block holds the sum of the two blocks directly below it, so fill the pyramid row by row from the bottom. Watch for students who add the whole bottom row once and forget that a middle number is used twice.

source: Use the same rule to fill these pyramids:
video_script.why: A child fills a number pyramid from the bottom row up, seeing each block as the sum of the two blocks below it.
video_script.substitution: the book's own three pyramids, filled row by row from the bottom
video_script.anchor: three number pyramids with only the bottom row filled
video_script.wrong_move: adds the whole bottom row once, forgetting that the middle number reaches the top by two paths
video_script.payoff_line: The tops are eight, fourteen and thirty two.
maths_rules: Bottom 5, 4, 5, 0: next row 9, 9, 5; then 18 and 14; top 18 + 14 = 32.
Doubt: 3 + 4 + 3 = 10 is not the top, because the 4 is used twice and 14 = 3 + 2 x 4 + 3.
video_script.design: One idea: each block holds the sum of the two blocks below it. The three pyramids stay in the anchor band and each is built on the working board.
open_questions: The book prints the three pyramids as figures that the text extract garbles; the bottom rows 6 2, 3 4 3 and 5 4 5 0 are taken from the worklist.

beats.on_screen: the small title card From your book appears; three pyramids stand with only their bottom rows filled and a rule card each block is the sum of the two blocks below it

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.pyr: three pyramids with filled bottom rows appear
marks.ask: the top block of each pyramid shows a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book. Each block of a number pyramid is the sum of the two blocks directly below it.
<bookmark mark='pyr'/>Here are three pyramids with only the bottom row filled.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What number goes in the top block of each?

beats.on_screen: the three pyramids hold still and the question marks glow

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a small pyramid: blocks 1 and 2 below, and arrows lead up to a block 3 above them

marks.rest: a block is shown resting on two blocks below it
marks.hold: the blocks 1 and 2 send arrows up to a block 3

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>A block rests on the two blocks directly below it.
<bookmark mark='hold'/>It holds their sum, so one and two below make three above.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three pyramids with the bottom rows below.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first has six and two.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second has three, four and three.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The third has five, four, five and zero.

beats.on_screen: To find: the top of each pyramid

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to fill each pyramid and find its top.

marks.rest: an arrow joins 6 and 2 to the top block
marks.top: 6 + 2 = 8 is written in the top block

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step one, in the first pyramid the top block rests on six and two.
<bookmark mark='top'/>Six plus two is eight.

marks.mid: 3 + 4 = 7 and 4 + 3 = 7 are written in the middle blocks
marks.top: 7 + 7 = 14 is written in the top block

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>Step two, in the second pyramid the middle blocks are three plus four, which is seven. The other is four plus three, which is also seven.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top is seven plus seven, which is fourteen.

marks.top: 18 + 14 = 32 is written in the top block

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>Step three, the third pyramid has four blocks at the bottom. The next row is nine, nine and five.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The row above is nine plus nine, which is eighteen, and nine plus five, which is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top is eighteen plus fourteen, which is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The tops are eight, fourteen and thirty two.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 3 + 4 + 3 = 10 on the second pyramid; two arrows run from the bottom 4 into both middle blocks; the bubble is struck out

marks.twice: two arrows run from the bottom 4 into both middle blocks
marks.strike: the bubble is struck out beside the real top 14

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the top is ten, by adding three, four and three.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Look at the bottom four. It sits under both middle blocks.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The four reaches the top by two paths, so ten is too small.
